intel.name: Nyasha's warning
intel.description: An encrypted voice message: a freight manifest, a date, and the sentence 'Never trust the people who send you.'

intel.name: Shadow Protocol archive fragment
intel.description: A partial file from the Directorate archive. It describes a deniable support network, a funding stream and a site called Kaguvi Hill.

intel.name: Nightjar cargo manifest
intel.description: A manifest for bay six: communications equipment, body armour, and a sealed container addressed to the Kaguvi Hill estate.

intel.name: The Ledger
intel.description: A handwritten and partly encrypted accounts book. It links Nightjar, a bureau de change at Eastgate, and a Directorate deputy director.

intel.name: Fingers' testimony
intel.description: A recorded statement from the bagman. He names Collin Mavhunga and describes the Kaguvi Hill payments.

intel.name: Chiweshe memo
intel.description: A ministry memo authorising a 'special liaison budget' for Nightjar. Rutendo Chiweshe's signature is on the last page.

intel.name: Mhofu's keycard
intel.description: A Nightjar access card, still warm. It opens the east service gate and the stairwell to the estate's private wing.

intel.name: Shadow Protocol core file
intel.description: The complete operational plan: a deniable network, a list of judges and officers on the payroll, and a contingency for 'post-electoral disruption'.

intel.name: Tariro's unpublished draft
intel.description: A 9,000-word investigation into Nightjar's government contracts. It needs one more named source. It might be you.

intel.name: Mukoma's route map
intel.description: A hand-drawn map of the old hunting paths around Kaguvi Hill, with a note: 'The fence has a blind spot at the dry riverbed.'

intel.name: Nightjar patrol schedule
intel.description: A copied duty roster showing when the Kaguvi Hill guards change shifts and which cameras go offline for maintenance.

witnesses.name: Tendai Chuma
witnesses.description: A young contract driver. He saw the manifest being loaded and knows the name of the man who signed it.

witnesses.name: Farai 'Fingers' Nyandoro
witnesses.description: The money launderer. He can connect the payments to Mavhunga, but only if he believes he will survive the week.

witnesses.name: Captain Dereck Mhofu
witnesses.description: The officer who runs Kaguvi Hill's security. He is not a true believer, but he is not a traitor either.

epilogues.title: The Sunlight Option
epilogues.text: By morning, the Shadow Protocol is a headline. Tariro's story runs with documents, testimony and a photograph of the Kaguvi Hill estate. The Directorate denies everything, then announces an internal review, then loses three senior officers to early retirement. Nightjar's contracts are suspended. Gumbo is found dead in a safehouse outside Nyanga, a pistol in his hand and no note. Mavhunga disappears. Kuda watches the news in a Mbare garage, drinking tea, waiting for the next thing. The truth is out. It does not make anyone safe. But it makes the next lie harder.

epilogues.title: The Quiet Option
epilogues.text: The Shadow Protocol changes hands. Mavhunga is arrested by officers who do not know they are arresting the wrong man. Gumbo retires to a farm in Mashonaland. Nightjar gets a new board and the same contracts. Kuda keeps the core file and a list of names. The Directorate gives him a desk, a budget and a title nobody outside the building will ever hear. Nyasha stops calling. Tariro publishes a story without his name and never speaks to him again. The country is calmer. The shadows are better organised.

epilogues.title: The Ash Option
epilogues.text: The estate burns for six hours. By the time the fire brigade reaches Kaguvi Hill, the archive room is a steel skeleton and the guest house is open to the sky. Gumbo is dead. Mavhunga is dead. The Shadow Protocol exists only in the memories of the people who built it. Tariro's story runs without documents. It is a good story. It changes nothing. Kuda walks away from the smoke with a burned hand and the names of the dead in his pocket. Zimbabwe is still standing. The truth is not.
